_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Bayer CropScience Ltd (standalone; no subsidiaries; Rs crore). One reportable segment (crop protection ~76%, hybrid corn seed ~19%, other ~5%). Revenue grows at a single rate; the business-line build (corn vs crop protection) is checked in the authoring script. EBITDA margin is a driver; treasury income = yield x opening cash and liquid funds net of lease liabilities. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
_revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 -4% (weather, lower acreage; corn held up); the June-September monsoon ended 12.6% below normal (IMD), kharif maize area ~4% below last year at 21-Aug and southern reservoirs ~33% below normal before a rabi season with El Nino expected to persist to Feb-2027; flubendiamide rights sold (Apr-2026). Q2FY26 was a weak base (excess rain, -11%), so we assume H1 about -3% and H2 about -3%. FY28-29: normal monsoons, corn seed +12-14% a year, crop protection +6-7% with launches (Bicota, Camalus, Etciostar, Xivana Smart, Plenexos later). Below management's 'high single to low double digit' aspiration; in line with its FY21-26 record of ~6% a year.

base._why: FY26 turnover Rs 5,675 cr split with the BRSR shares (corn seed 19%, crop protection 76% + other 5%); rounded, so approximate.

businessLines._why: Corn: Q1FY27 held up despite ~4% lower kharif maize area; rabi risk from southern reservoirs; then +13% a year (FY21-25: ~15%; management: double again over ~5 years). Crop protection and other: -4.9% in FY27 (deficient monsoon, flubendiamide rights sold, older products divested), then +6-7% with launches. The authoring script checks that the two lines sum to model revenue.

_marginWhy: 15.4% in FY26 (12.6% in FY25, 18-19% in FY23-24 when glyphosate prices spiked). Q1FY27 20.0% (18.2%) on price increases and mix. Management guided ~+100bp a year from FY25 for 2-3 years and has already delivered +280bp; more local sourcing, lower receivable write-offs and the partner go-to-market model help, but a falling top line in FY27 and Chinese generic pricing cap it. We stay below the FY20-24 average (~18.6%).
_capexWhy: Cash capex Rs 43-77 cr a year in FY22-26 (Rs 64 cr in FY26, incl. Rs 39 cr of R&D capital) plus Rs 26-107 cr a year of new leased assets (warehouses, vehicles), which depreciate like capex. We include ~Rs 40 cr a year of leases so depreciation does not fall artificially.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs 94 cr (incl. Rs 55 cr on right-of-use assets) = 10.4% of average gross block (Rs 902 cr, Screener).
_treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash and liquid funds net of lease liabilities (Rs 1,397 cr at Mar-26). March is the seasonal peak; cash falls through the year as dealers are given credit and two dividends are paid. FY26 treasury income (deposit interest Rs 32.5 cr + mutual-fund gains Rs 15.6 cr) was ~5.9% of the opening net balance.
_otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: rent from group companies (~Rs 13 cr) and penal interest on overdue dealer receivables (~Rs 10 cr) recur; FY27 adds the Rs 63.9 cr gain on selling the flubendiamide marketing rights (Q1FY27). Profit on divesting products (Rs 22-27 cr a year in FY25-26) is not assumed to recur.
_interestWhy: Rs 20 cr in FY26: lease interest (Rs 8 cr) and interest on employee benefits/MSME dues; no borrowings.
_taxWhy: Effective 19.4% in FY26 and 19.7% in FY25: income from producing corn seed is claimed as tax-exempt agricultural income (Rs 64.6 cr tax saving in FY26), under dispute (Rs 233 cr contingent).
_payoutWhy: Dividends were 77-105% of EPS in FY22-26 (Rs 150 a share for FY26, ~98%); management said the dividend distribution 'remains intact' through the FY25 dip. The promoter group (71.4%) receives ~71% of it.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free with net cash; earnings swing with the monsoon but the parent's support and dividend record lower the risk: slightly below market sensitivity (Ke 11.6%).
dcf._tgWhy: Indian crop protection and seed demand grows with farm output and prices; 5.5% nominal, below the 6% we use for faster-growing peers because ~95% of profit is paid out.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Industry growth of 5-6% plus corn seed share gains.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Asset-light formulator and seed producer: capex (incl. leases) ~2% of sales.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: A normal rabi and 2027 monsoon; corn seed keeps growing ~15% and new molecules (Xivana Smart, Plenexos) scale; local sourcing lifts gross margin; margin ~18%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: El Nino hurts the rabi and the 2027 kharif; glyphosate use restricted; Chinese generic prices fall again and receivable write-offs return; margin ~15%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Bayer CropScience (HSBC 29x FY27E EPS; Kotak method not disclosed). 24x = its 31.7x one-year-forward median since Apr-2021, cut by the ~20% de-rating of domestic crop-protection peers (Sumitomo, PI, Dhanuka, Rallis) to ~25.5x, and by ~5% because our FY26-29E EPS growth (~6%) is a little below the ~7% it delivered while trading at 31.7x. Bull 28x (its 25th percentile since 2021); bear 19x (dividend-discount value at an 11.6% cost of equity).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Values the business and the net cash separately. 16x Sep-28E EBITDA = its ~25x trailing EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021, less the same ~20% de-rating and ~5% growth discount (~19x trailing), restated on EBITDA two years ahead (+18%).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.6%, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash.
